12-050.r: Order of formation: Rajasthan (earliest) → Maharashtra 1960 → Haryana 1966; so descending (latest first) = Haryana, Maharashtra, Rajasthan.
12-050.t: Descending means latest first; don't write the earliest-first order.

12-051.r: Statehood: Nagaland 1963 (16th State, 1 December); Sikkim 1975; Jharkhand 15 November 2000; Telangana 2 June 2014.
12-051.c: Option (b) matches if Nagaland's year is taken as 1962, when the State of Nagaland Act was passed; the book marks none because Nagaland became a State on 1 December 1963.

12-052.r: Chronology: Nagaland (1 Dec 1963, 16th State) → Punjab (1 Nov 1966, Punjab Reorganisation Act) → Sikkim (16 May 1975, 22nd State) → Arunachal Pradesh.

12-053.r: Himachal Pradesh: province 15 April 1948, State 25 January 1971; West Bengal, Punjab, Assam: provinces 1947, States 26 January 1950. No 'State' formed in 1948.
12-053.c: Book prints no answer: none became a State in 1948; Himachal Pradesh fits only if 'province' was meant.

12-054.r: Mysore was renamed Karnataka (1973), not Tamil Nadu; Goa separated from Daman and Diu 1987; Bombay split into Gujarat and Maharashtra 1960; Himachal (ex-UT) became State 1971.

12-055.r: States Reorganisation Commission (language basis) set up 29 December 1953; report 30 September 1955; chair Fazal Ali, members K.M. Panikkar, H.N. Kunzru → States Reorganisation Act 1956.
12-055.t: Don't confuse 1953 (Commission set up) with 1956 (States Reorganisation Act passed).

12-056.r: Fazl Ali Commission (SRC, 1953): chair Justice Syed Fazl Ali; members K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru. K.T. Shah and Pattabhi Sitaramayya were not members.
12-056.h: F-P-K trio: Fazl Ali, Panikkar, Kunzru.

12-057.r: SRC (1953) = Justice Fazal Ali (chair), K.M. Panikkar, Hridaynath Kunzru; not Tej Bahadur Sapru or Pattabhi Sitaramayya. Report September 1955: language accepted as broad basis.

12-059.r: First linguistic State: Andhra Pradesh, October 1953; large-scale reorganisation of States on linguistic basis in 1956.

12-062.r: Andhra Pradesh (October 1953) → first State formed on language basis, by separating Telugu-speaking areas from Madras State.
12-062.h: Andhra = 'A' for first; Telugu areas cut from Madras.

12-064.r: SRC (Fazal Ali, Panikkar, Kunzru; report September 1955) did not support splitting Bombay and Punjab. States Reorganisation Act 1956 → 14 States and 6 centrally administered territories.
12-064.t: Statement II is false: the SRC did not back splitting Bombay or Punjab.

12-066.r: Per book, Andhra Pradesh's capital was not renamed; renamed: Madras → Chennai, Calcutta → Kolkata, Bombay → Mumbai, Bangalore → Bengaluru, Pondicherry → Puducherry.
12-066.c: The explanation points to (d) Andhra Pradesh: Madras, Calcutta and Trivandrum were renamed, Hyderabad was not. Andhra Pradesh's capital is now Amaravati.

12-067.r: Both true: after Nagpur Session 1920 (C. Vijayaraghavachariar), Congress committees formed on linguistic basis; 1948 (S.K. Dhar Commission, JVP Committee) Congress rejected linguistic provinces.

13-001.r: Citizenship → Part II of the Constitution, Articles 5 to 11.

13-004.r: India → single citizenship for the whole country; USA → dual citizenship (of the federation and of a state).

13-006.r: Citizenship Act 1955 → citizenship by Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, Incorporation of territory; never by depositing money in Indian banks.
13-006.h: Better Dads Raise Nice Indians = Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, Incorporation.

13-007.r: Loss of citizenship (Citizenship Act 1955): renunciation, termination, deprivation. Renouncing or voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship ends it; marrying a foreigner or criticising government does not.

13-008.r: India: one citizenship and one domicile (from UK). Any citizen, by birth or naturalised, can become President; a naturalised citizen can be deprived of citizenship.

13-009.r: OCI cardholder (Section 7A, Citizenship Act 1955): not for an Indian who migrated to Pakistan after Partition; minor child, foreign spouse, specified great-grandchild are eligible.
hi: Overseas Citizen of India (प्रवासी भारतीय नागरिक)

13-010.r: Articles 371A to 371I → special provisions for Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa. USA dual citizenship, India single; naturalised citizen can be deprived.

13-011.r: Dual citizenship → USA: citizen of the USA and of the state where he resides. India has single citizenship.

13-012.r: Article 11 → Parliament regulates citizenship by law → Citizenship Act 1955; Central Government made Citizenship Rules 2009 under Section 18.

13-013.r: Registration under Section 5(1)(a), Citizenship Act 1955 → a person of Indian origin must ordinarily reside in India for 7 years.

13-014.r: Only Parliament (Article 11) has exclusive power over citizenship; Central Government only frames rules under Section 18, Citizenship Act 1955.
13-014.c: Book marks none: Article 11 gives this power to Parliament as a whole, not to the Lok Sabha alone; the Central Government only frames rules under the Act.

13-015.r: Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2019: Lok Sabha 9 December; Rajya Sabha 11 December 2019 (passed by Parliament); President's assent 12 December 2019.
13-015.t: Don't confuse 11 December (Parliament passed) with 12 December (President's assent).

13-017.r: CAA 2019 → citizenship for persecuted Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, Christians from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan who entered India before end of December 2014.
13-017.h: Three neighbours A-B-P: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan; six non-Muslim communities.

14-001.r: Best safeguard of liberty in a liberal democracy → separation of powers (restrains power); not a committed judiciary or centralisation.

14-002.r: Fundamental Rights resolution → Karachi Session 1931 (26-31 March, president Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel), with National Economic Programme; endorsed Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

14-003.r: Nehru Report (1928) advocated including Fundamental Rights in the Constitution; not GoI Act 1935, August Offer 1940 or Cripps Mission 1942.

14-004.r: Jawaharlal Nehru: a Fundamental Right should be seen not from any moment's difficulty but as something to make permanent in the Constitution.

14-005.r: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan: Fundamental Rights are 'a pledge to our people and a pact with the civilized world'.

14-006.r: Fundamental Rights are justiciable: enforceable by courts, subject to certain restrictions.

14-007.r: Called Fundamental because written in the Constitution, essential for personality development, and Parliament can't make laws against them (basic structure).

14-008.r: Fundamental Rights can be suspended only during Emergency (Articles 358, 359); Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended.
14-008.h: 20-21 never done: Articles 20 and 21 survive every Emergency.

14-009.r: Fundamental Rights: guarantee against State action; listed in Part III; help ensure social, economic, political justice (mostly via DPSP, Part IV); they resemble the US Bill of Rights.

14-010.r: Fundamental Rights → Part III, Articles 12 to 35; six Fundamental Rights for citizens.

14-011.r: Article 13 → pre- or post-Constitution laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void to that extent; secures paramountcy of the Constitution on Fundamental Rights.
14-011.t: Article 245 = extent of laws by Parliament and States; Article 326 = elections to Lok Sabha.

14-013.r: Right to Equality → Articles 14 to 18: 14 equality before law; 15 no discrimination; 16 public employment; 17 untouchability abolished; 18 titles abolished.

14-014.r: Right to Equality = Articles 14 to 18, so Articles 14, 15, 16 are included; Article 13 is not part of it.

14-015.r: Article 14 → equality before law and equal protection of laws for every person (citizen or foreigner); puts a limitation on legislative power.

14-017.r: Equal protection of laws → Article 14 (concept from the American Constitution); with equality before law; for citizens and foreigners.

14-018.r: A law giving the executive unguided, uncontrolled discretionary power → violates Article 14 (ultra vires).

14-019.r: Rule of Law → one law for all and one judiciary for all; no one, however highly placed, is above the law.

14-020.r: Article 15 (no discrimination on religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth) falls under Right to Equality (Articles 14-18).

14-021.r: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan → First Amendment (1951) added Article 15(4): special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes.

14-022.r: Article 15(5) → reservation in admission to educational institutions, including private aided or unaided ones (not minority institutions), for SC, ST and backward classes.

14-023.r: OBC reservation → Article 15(4) (special provisions for backward classes, SC, ST) and Article 16(4) (reservation in appointments or posts for backward classes).

14-024.r: Article 16(2) → no citizen barred from State employment on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence.
14-024.t: Article 15 lists religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth only; 'descent' and 'residence' appear in Article 16(2).

14-025.r: Equality of opportunity in public employment for all citizens → Article 16(1) and 16(2).

14-026.r: Right to Equality covers equality before law (Article 14), social equality (Article 15), equal opportunity (Article 16); not economic equality.

14-027.r: Both A and R true, R explains A: Article 14 permits reasonable classification to treat unequals differently, but among equals law must be equal and equally administered.

14-028.r: SC: reservation under Article 16(4) is limited by Article 335 (efficiency of administration); but Article 335 does not define 'efficiency of administration'.

14-029.r: 77th Amendment Act, 1995 → inserted Article 16(4A): reservation in promotion for SC and ST.
